pos.personaBrief: Inter had under 40% of the ball in the 3-1 win over Barcelona and attacked quickly after winning it back, and the team won while giving up possession. Low confidence for the season as a whole: the evidence is one tier C analysis.

pro.personaBrief: The team attacked quickly after regaining the ball and was quick in transition with Eto'o, Milito and Pandev up front. No build-up evidence (a gap), so playing out short under pressure is inferred to be unlikely.

est.personaBrief: A rehearsed shape (the 'gabbia' mid-block, width given up for compactness, a 4-2-3-1 with clearly labelled roles in the final) points to well-defined positions, while Milito combined with Sneijder rather than waiting in the box.

lar.personaBrief: Mourinho sacrificed offensive width for defensive compactness and used wide forwards (Eto'o, Pandev) as workers, with Sneijder central. Width came mainly from Maicon at full-back, not from wingers hugging the line.

blo.personaBrief: The first leg was a mid-block and Inter dropped back quickly on defensive transitions; the paraphrased goal of moving the line 20 metres forward suggests mid rather than ultra-deep, but there was no high press.

mar.personaBrief: Mourinho says Messi was stopped by shared responsibility, 'not man to man' (attributed, 2022), while the Substack analysis says he was man-marked; I weight the manager's stated zonal intent with collective pressure on the star. Corner marking is unverified.

pla.personaBrief: The Barcelona plan was built entirely around 'not letting Messi play', and the system shifted to a 4-2-3-1 mid-season: an opponent-driven, adaptable game plan.

res.personaBrief: A treble won with under 40% of the ball and a compact block against Barcelona, plus Eto'o filling in at full-back after Motta's red card, shows a purely result-first purpose.

sis.personaBrief: Stars such as Eto'o accepted defensive work, even as an auxiliary full-back, and everyone shared responsibility for Messi: the collective system decided, and talent served it.

jog.personaBrief: No verified evidence for this axis: these answers come from general knowledge of a physical, experienced side (Lucio, Samuel, Cambiasso, Zanetti), kept consistent with its intense defensive transitions and its hounding of Barcelona in midfield.

bas.personaBrief: The starting line-up in the final averaged just under 30, and Mourinho got everything out of a vastly experienced, ageing squad assembled through signings.

lid.personaBrief: No verified evidence for this axis: these answers come from general knowledge of Mourinho's Inter, with firm authority (e.g. disciplining Balotelli) combined with a strongly united, loyal group, consistent with players like Eto'o accepting sacrificial roles.
